title: Dima and Magic Guitar
statementMd:
Dima loves Inna very much. He decided to write a song for her. Dima has a magic guitar with $*n*$ strings and $*m*$ frets. Dima makes the guitar produce sounds like that: to play a note, he needs to hold one of the strings on one of the frets and then pull the string. When Dima pulls the $*i*$-th string holding it on the $*j*$-th fret the guitar produces a note, let's denote it as $*a*_{*ij*}$. We know that Dima's guitar can produce $*k*$ distinct notes. It is possible that some notes can be produced in multiple ways. In other words, it is possible that $*a*_{*ij*} = *a*_{*pq*}$ at $(*i*, *j*) ≠ (*p*, *q*)$.

Dima has already written a song — a sequence of $*s*$ notes. In order to play the song, you need to consecutively produce the notes from the song on the guitar. You can produce each note in any available way. Dima understood that there are many ways to play a song and he wants to play it so as to make the song look as complicated as possible (try to act like Cobein).

We'll represent a way to play a song as a sequence of pairs $(*x*_{*i*}, *y*_{*i*})$ $(1 ≤ *i* ≤ *s*)$, such that the $*x*_{*i*}$-th string on the $*y*_{*i*}$-th fret produces the $*i*$-th note from the song. The complexity of moving between pairs $(*x*_{1}, *y*_{1})$ and $(*x*_{2}, *y*_{2})$ equals ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8a0451c828fe05943c3ac315333f3470def44351.png) + ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/360d86bbf189f569f8236074a6b88335a9606c04.png). The complexity of a way to play a song is the maximum of complexities of moving between adjacent pairs.

Help Dima determine the maximum complexity of the way to play his song! The guy's gotta look cool!

## Input

The first line of the input contains four integers $*n*$, $*m*$, $*k*$ and $*s*$ $(1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 2000, 1 ≤ *k* ≤ 9, 2 ≤ *s* ≤ 10^{5})$.

Then follow $*n*$ lines, each containing $*m*$ integers $*a*_{*ij*}$ $(1 ≤ *a*_{*ij*} ≤ *k*)$. The number in the $*i*$-th row and the $*j*$-th column ($*a*_{*ij*}$) means a note that the guitar produces on the $*i*$-th string and the $*j*$-th fret.

The last line of the input contains $*s*$ integers $*q*_{*i*}$ $(1 ≤ *q*_{*i*} ≤ *k*)$ — the sequence of notes of the song.

## Output

In a single line print a single number — the maximum possible complexity of the song.
statementZhMd:
Dima 非常爱 Inna。他决定为她写一首歌。Dima 有一把拥有 $*n*$ 根弦和 $*m*$ 个品的魔法吉他。Dima 让吉他发出声音的方式如下：演奏一个音符时，他需要在某根弦的某个品上按住弦，然后拨动琴弦。当 Dima 按住第 $*i*$ 根弦的第 $*j*$ 个品并拨动琴弦时，吉他会发出一个音符，我们将其记为 $*a*_{*ij*}$。已知 Dima 的吉他可以发出 $*k*$ 种不同的音符。同一个音符可能有多种演奏方式。换句话说，可能存在 $(*i*, *j*) ≠ (*p*, *q*)$，但 $*a*_{*ij*} = *a*_{*pq*}$。

Dima 已经写好了一首歌——由 $*s*$ 个音符组成的序列。为了演奏这首歌，需要在吉他上依次演奏歌曲中的音符。每个音符都可以用任意一种可行方式演奏。Dima 发现演奏这首歌有很多种方式，他希望选择一种方式，使这首歌看起来尽可能复杂（试着表现得像 Cobein 一样）。

我们将一种演奏歌曲的方式表示为一个数对序列 $(*x*_{*i*}, *y*_{*i*})$ $(1 ≤ *i* ≤ *s*)$，其中第 $*x*_{*i*}$ 根弦的第 $*y*_{*i*}$ 个品能够发出歌曲中的第 $*i*$ 个音符。从数对 $(*x*_{1}, *y*_{1})$ 移动到数对 $(*x*_{2}, *y*_{2})$ 的复杂度等于 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8a0451c828fe05943c3ac315333f3470def44351.png) + ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/360d86bbf189f569f8236074a6b88335a9606c04.png)。一种演奏方式的复杂度定义为相邻数对之间移动复杂度的最大值。

请帮助 Dima 确定演奏这首歌时可能达到的最大复杂度！这家伙必须看起来很酷！

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含四个整数 $*n*$、$*m*$、$*k*$ 和 $*s*$ $(1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 2000, 1 ≤ *k* ≤ 9, 2 ≤ *s* ≤ 10^{5})$。

接下来有 $*n*$ 行，每行包含 $*m*$ 个整数 $*a*_{*ij*}$ $(1 ≤ *a*_{*ij*} ≤ *k*)$。第 $*i*$ 行第 $*j*$ 列的数 $*a*_{*ij*}$ 表示吉他在第 $*i*$ 根弦的第 $*j*$ 个品上发出的音符。

输入的最后一行包含 $*s*$ 个整数 $*q*_{*i*}$ $(1 ≤ *q*_{*i*} ≤ *k*)$，表示歌曲的音符序列。

## 输出格式

在一行中输出一个整数——演奏这首歌时可能达到的最大复杂度。
